chapter.title: Sorting items down two belts

cards.body:
Picture a worker standing where the belt forks in two. Every box that reaches them gets one glance at one label, say a red *urgent* sticker, and one push: red goes left to the hot line, no red goes right to the normal line.

**One check, two belts, and every box ends up on exactly one of them.** Nothing stops, nothing gets binned.
cards.simpler:
Imagine a worker standing where a conveyor belt splits in two. Each box that arrives gets one quick look at one label. If it has a red urgent sticker, the worker pushes it left to the fast line. If not, it goes right to the normal line.

**One check, two belts, and every box lands on exactly one of them.** Nothing waits and nothing gets thrown away.

cards.prompt: A box reaches the fork station. The worker's only instruction is: 'fragile sticker goes left, everything else goes right.' What happens to a box with no sticker at all?

options.text: It waits at the fork until someone adds a sticker.
It goes right, with everything else that is not fragile.
It gets thrown in the bin for failing the check.

whyNot.a: That's a jam, not a sort: the fork never holds a box, it always sends each one somewhere.
whyNot.c: That's the Filter station's habit, not the fork's: the fork keeps every box and gives it a belt.

cards.reteach: The fork asks one yes-or-no question about each box. Yes goes one way, no goes the other. 'No sticker' is just a no, so the box rides the normal belt.

cards.title: The IF node asks one question
cards.body:
In n8n the fork is the *IF node*. You give it one condition made of three parts: a field, a comparison, and a value. For example: the field priority, the comparison *is equal to*, the value urgent.

Every item that arrives gets checked on its own. Items where the answer is yes leave through the output labelled *true*. All the others leave through the output labelled *false*.

**Both outputs are real exits.** You can drag a node onto either one. The IF node never deletes anything. It only decides which door each item walks out of.
cards.simpler:
In n8n, the fork is the IF node. You give it one question with three parts: a field, a comparison, and a value. For example: the field priority, the comparison is equal to, the value urgent.

Each item gets checked by itself. Items that match leave through the exit marked true. The rest leave through the exit marked false.

**Both exits are real doors.** The IF node never throws anything away. It only picks which door each item uses.

cards.title: The ticket that shouted
cards.body:
Say a support form feeds your workflow, and a field called urgency holds either urgent or normal. You add an IF node: urgency is equal to urgent. True goes to Slack, false goes to Google Sheets.

You run it on 9 test responses. 8 sort perfectly. One lands on the false side even though the customer plainly meant it: they typed URGENT in capitals. The IF node compares text exactly, so URGENT and urgent are two different words to it. Tick the *Ignore Case* option in the node and the shouting customer gets routed with the rest.
cards.simpler:
A support form feeds the workflow. Its urgency field holds either urgent or normal. You add an IF node: urgency is equal to urgent. True goes to Slack, false goes to Google Sheets.

You test 9 responses and 8 sort correctly. One lands on the false side. They typed URGENT in capitals. **The IF node compares text exactly**, so URGENT and urgent count as two different words. Tick Ignore Case in the node and that customer sorts with the rest.

cards.prompt: You want urgent form responses to post in a Slack channel and every other response to land in a spreadsheet. Which setup does that?

options.text: A Filter node set to urgency is equal to urgent, with Slack and Sheets both connected after it.
An IF node set to urgency is equal to urgent, Slack on the true output, Sheets on the false output.
Two IF nodes in a row, the first checking for urgent and the second checking for normal.

whyNot.a: That's a Filter, not a fork: the normal responses get dropped before they ever reach Sheets.
whyNot.c: That's two forks where one does the job: the first IF node's false output already holds every non-urgent item.

cards.reteach: One IF node gives you two doors. Put what you want for urgent items behind the true door, and what you want for everyone else behind the false door. One check, both groups handled.

cards.title: Filter: the station with a bin
cards.body:
The *Filter node* looks like IF but has one exit. Items that pass the condition carry on. Items that fail are dropped from the run, and n8n lists them in a *discarded* tab so you can see what went.

Pick between them with one question: does the other group need anything done? If yes, use IF. If the other group can simply vanish, use Filter.

**The IF node checks items one at a time.** Send 10 in and you might get 3 out of true and 7 out of false. If one side gets zero items, the nodes behind that door just do not run this time. That is normal, not an error.
cards.simpler:
The Filter node looks like IF but has one exit. Passing items carry on. Failing items are dropped, and n8n shows them in a discarded tab.

To choose, ask: does the other group need anything done? If yes, use IF. If not, use Filter.

**The IF node checks items one at a time.** Send 10 in and maybe 3 go true and 7 go false. If one side gets nothing, the nodes behind that door skip this run. That is normal.

cards.body:
Sam builds an IF node, drags a Slack node onto the true output, runs it, and gets 2 messages from 11 responses. Where did the other 9 go? They are sitting at the false output with nothing connected, delivered to a door nobody opened.

**Spot it by clicking the IF node and opening the false tab in its output panel.** If the count there is not zero, something is waiting for you.
cards.simpler:
Sam builds an IF node, connects a Slack node to the true exit, runs it, and gets 2 messages from 11 responses. Where did the other 9 go? They are sitting at the false exit with nothing connected. They were delivered to a door nobody opened.

**Spot it by clicking the IF node and opening the false tab in its output panel.** If the count there is not zero, something is waiting for you.

cards.prompt: 12 expense claims arrive. An IF node checks: amount is greater than 500. 4 claims pass. What happens to the other 8?

options.text: They are removed from the run and show up in a discarded tab.
They leave through the false output and wait for whatever you connect there.
They go back to the trigger and get checked again on the next run.

whyNot.a: That's what the Filter node does, not IF: a Filter has a bin, an IF node has a second door.
whyNot.c: That's not how the belt moves: items only travel forward, and the IF node has already given each one a door.

cards.reteach: An IF node sorts, it never removes. Every item comes out of exactly one of its two outputs. 4 went true, so 8 went false, and they are only as lost as the empty space after that output.

cards.title: In one breath
cards.body: **An IF node asks one yes-or-no question about each item and sends it out the true door or the false door, keeping every item.** A Filter node asks the same question but drops the no's, so use it only when the no's can disappear.
cards.simpler: **An IF node asks one yes-or-no question about each item and sends it out the true door or the false door, keeping every item.** A Filter node asks the same question but throws away the no's. Use Filter only when the no's can disappear. Think of a sorting worker versus a worker with a bin.

cards.body: Open a workflow from an earlier chapter and add an IF node after the first node. Set one condition on a field you can see. Run it, then click the true and false tabs and count the items on each side.
cards.simpler: Open a workflow you built in an earlier chapter. Add an IF node right after the first node. Give it one condition on a field you can actually see in the data. Run the workflow. Then click the true tab and the false tab and **count how many items landed on each side.**

chapter.outcomeLine: You can now route items down two different paths based on one field's value.
